1: Tidewall Climbing: six gyms, about forty million a year, a term loan, and one promise to the bank: net leverage under three times EBITDA. Two AI agents, an analyst named Maya, and a controller named Dana run finance.
2: April 9. The billing system publishes its March export: every member, every dollar released into revenue.
3: April 10. The Close Accountant closes Q1 on it: revenue by gym, EBITDA, trailing EBITDA of 5.6 million. Fifty-one pieces of work, each logging the rows it read.
4: The Covenant agent builds on those: leverage 2.95, the certificate to the bank, bonuses, the tax payment. Maya builds the board deck on top with the same tools, so her reads are logged too. That's the context graph.
5: July 8. Tidewall turns on Trackback. First job: compare today's export with the version everyone read. Five gyms, one month, 118,000 dollars counted twice. Now: what else is wrong?
6: Here's what runs. Diff the two versions. Follow the read logs to the work that used those rows; nothing else is touched. Recompute each number from its formula. Apply Dana's materiality memo: small moves stop, a flipped conclusion never does. Sentences: refresh the figure if the claim holds; otherwise, back to the author. Forty-four of 174 checked; the rest cleared, with reasons.
7: Each affected agent gets one message, about only what it used; Maya gets the same as a notice. Your certificate rests on net leverage, now 3.03, over your 3.00 covenant. Still valid? It can't un-send a certificate, so it drafts a corrected one for the CFO. Maya rewrites three deck sentences. The cash forecast: untouched, so nobody's asked.
8: The agent's write-up called this immaterial: under five percent. Jade, the reviewer, re-checks every call against the engines: over performance materiality, covenant breached, bonuses already paid. Overruled. Jade doesn't write numbers; she checks them.
9: Every fix goes to the role that can sign it: certificate to the CFO, bonuses to HR, entries to the controller. Dana rejects the first entry: it's dated into locked Q1. The agent re-drafts in June, tagged to March. Try to self-approve? The database rejects the row.
10: Jade's overrule and Dana's no become proposed lessons. Before one goes live, it's re-run against every past case. The broad version fails: three old cases would flip. The rest pass; Dana approves; playbook v2. Held-out cases: eighty percent to one hundred.
11: And the record: what the agent could see on April 10, duplicates included. Ask for July 8 from that date: refused, with both timestamps.
12: It's live. The link opens in Deep mode on this company, with a tour. Drop the correction yourself. Trackback traces any correction forward.
